rule: MDD at 80% power and two-sided alpha 0.05 (and at the first Holm step of its family) for 52 tasks, Hermes and OpenClaw pooled, 3 gstack and 3 no-gstack attempts per task: (z(1-alpha/2) + z(0.8)) x sqrt(sum over harnesses of v (1/3 + 1/3) / (52 x 2^2)), v the mean per-task variance k(n-k)/(n(n-1)). The lift difference adds the two models' variance sums. Same formula as scripts/frontier-harbor/analyze.ts expectedMdd with lift_sd 0.

frontier.what: per-task variances of the frontier harness run (frontier-harness-2026-11), merged trials.jsonl with its lookup-fails list, from bun scripts/frontier-harbor/analyze.ts mdd --tasks 52 --attempts 3 --baseline-attempts 3 --lift-sd 0

particle-1.what: uncounted checks before this preregistration: the first 6 tasks of the shared order, 3 trials per task per harness (installed, start-hook and told arms pooled). Hermes per-task variance 0.1667 (passes per task 1, 3, 3, 0, 2, 1 of 3); OpenClaw 0 (3, 3, 3, 0, 3, 3 of 3), floored at the frontier models value because 0 from 6 tasks is too low

borrowed_variance.label: GPT-6.2 Sol
borrowed_variance.why: GPT-6.2 Sol has no trials on these 52 tasks in any earlier run, so the sol rows here use GPT-6.1 Sol's per-task variances from the frontier harness run (the sol-hermes and sol-openclaw cells above), and the reach row uses the GPT-6.1 Sol minus Opus gap. The run's own MDD for GPT-6.2 Sol comes from its trials, in gstack-analysis.json.

lift_difference.why: the lift difference MDD at the estimates is at most 10 points

reach.what: particle-1 with gstack minus a frontier model without. Its noise is dominated by how two models differ task by task, estimated from the per-task Sol minus Opus gap (no gstack, Hermes and OpenClaw pooled, 2 attempts) in the frontier harness run
